A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAGRouter work despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing-accuracy and latency experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and retrieval-noise evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds stronger-model comparisons, failure analysis, cross-domain evaluations, and summarization experiments.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix H introduces score-based probabilistic label sampling for WikiASP: a normalized continuous score s produces a positive training label with probability s and a negative label with probability 1-s. This extends v1's binary-correctness supervision. The original architecture, contrastive objectives, and routing procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 retains the five original QA datasets and adds HotpotQA multi-hop QA and WikiASP aspect-based summarization. Appendix F also introduces medical-to-Wikipedia QA and search-QA-to-medical transfer scenarios, substantially extending task requirements and domain-shift coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-Max, and DeepSeek-R1 as individually evaluated model comparators. GPT-4o previously served inside the Prompt LLM routing baseline rather than as a candidate answerer. The routing comparators in the retained experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a six-model candidate pool for the NQ/WebQ comparison, two cross-domain training/testing protocols, and ROUGE-L evaluation for summarization. Its failure analysis excludes cases where all candidate LLMs fail and categorizes the remaining failures. Original QA sample counts, metrics, and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an ablation of the RAG Capability Embedding Layer, quantitative failure categories and analysis of cases where baselines succeed but RAGRouter fails, and cross-domain generalization tests. The original retrieval-noise analysis, sensitivity sweeps, and two successful routing examples remain; moving their displays does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice; probabilistic training-label sampling is not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Retained results are unchanged, including Table 2's 64.46% average accuracy. New results include 59.38% versus GPT-4o's 57.71% in Table 3, 63.70% without RAG capability embeddings, a 12.95% failure rate in Table 12, cross-domain accuracies of 21.20% and 68.89%, and WikiASP ROUGE-L of 0.1981 versus KNN Router's 0.1881. These are additional results under distinct settings, not improvements over corresponding v1 scores.

T1.justification: Appendix H adds a limited mathematical extension to training-label construction: continuous scores define positive and negative label probabilities s and 1-s. The original routing formulation, loss equations, and response-reversal definitions in Equations 1–11 remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the effectiveness claim to open- and closed-source candidate models. The abstract drops v1's specific improvement figures, while the introduction reports a broader 1.67%–9.33% improvement range. The central novelty, knowledge-shift modeling, and latency-trade-off claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting transfer performance to learned relative RAG capabilities and residual failures to retrieval-induced degradation, task difficulty, and model-selection overconfidence. It interprets the new embedding ablation as supporting separate capability modeling. v1's discussion of future applications beyond RAG is removed, while the central knowledge-shift explanation is retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code/data repository link, extends API-access disclosure to the added models, and explains the single-embedding ablation configuration and probabilistic supervision. Existing implementation settings remain unchanged. Inference-cost measurements move from v1 Appendix G to v2 Section 5.2; they are not newly reported.

R1.justification: v2 adds the WikiASP and HotpotQA references and removes citations concerning distillation, parameter-efficient transfer learning, LoRA, and chain-of-thought prompting alongside the deleted future-work discussion. Related-work positioning against non-RAG-aware routers remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, edits selected abstract, contribution, and architecture passages, and reorganizes experimental and appendix subsections. It adds appendix contents and funding acknowledgments and moves inference-cost discussion into the main text. Most original prose and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation expands with tables for stronger-model comparisons, failure categories, cross-domain transfer, and summarization. v1's combined ablation table becomes separate architecture and contrastive-learning tables. Existing sensitivity heatmaps move into the main text, and appendix figures and case tables are regrouped; these retained figures are not new analyses.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by directly testing the distinctive RAG capability embedding, quantifying routing failures, and examining transfer beyond the original QA settings through stronger candidate models, cross-domain tests, and summarization. These additions address important gaps in mechanism attribution and applicability while preserving the original evidence. HotpotQA/WikiASP setup details remain incomplete and statistical uncertainty remains unreported, limiting the strength of the expanded generalization claims.
